ai.description: Roland's Burrowing Frog reaches 3–4 cm. It is brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark flank markings. Key features include a shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercle and a blunt, rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sphaerotheca rolandae* is best distinguished by its distinct, shovel-shaped inner metatarsal tubercle, which is significantly larger and more prominent than in similar species.
ai.habitat: Roland's Burrowing Frog inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations near seasonal pools.
ai.behavior: Roland's Burrowing Frog is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its powerful hind limbs to rapidly dig backward into sandy soil to hide from predators or escape heat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphaerotheca rolandae* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of eggs in temporary pools. It follows an explosive breeding strategy typical of burrowing frogs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sphaerotheca rolandae* is found in the Indian subcontinent, primarily across the Deccan Plateau and parts of the Western Ghats, ranging from sea level to mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: Roland's Burrowing Frog produces a low-pitched, repetitive "tok-tok" call. It is typically heard during the monsoon season near temporary rain pools and flooded fields.
